data.narrative:
Parallel Systems is a Series A-stage transportation company founded by Matt Soule, John Howard, and Ben Stabler that has raised $100M to date. The broader transportation sector includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, FleetZero among them) and no directly comparable public benchmarks.

Given the nascent stage and heterogeneous peer landscape, a Stage-Progression method provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A-to-later-stage progression yields an implied value of $12M. A Peer-Median approach was not applicable: while 3 same-sector peers exist in transportation, none satisfied minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filtering, making a narrow peer comparison unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M (median $12M). Key uncertainties center on the absence of tightly filtered peer comparables and the reliance on a single quantitative method. Stage-progression multiples vary meaningfully by investor sentiment and sector cycle dynamics; this 2.0x assumption warrants sensitivity testing. The $100M already deployed also raises questions about burn rate, runway, and whether capital efficiency meets Series A-stage expectations for this sector. Additional transparency on revenue traction or unit economics would materially strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this range.
